hechos/revolucion-hungara-de-1956/resume.texto: Popular uprising of October 1956 against the communist regime and the Soviet presence; Imre Nagy's government announced its withdrawal from the Warsaw Pact. The Soviet army crushed it in November, with some 2,500 Hungarians killed and some 200,000 refugees.

hechos/independencia-de-ghana/resumen.texto: On March 6, 1957, the British colony of the Gold Coast became independent under the name Ghana, with Kwame Nkrumah as head of government. It was the first colony in sub-Saharan Africa to do so and opened the wave of African independence.

hechos/gran-salto-adelante/resumen.texto: Mao's campaign to industrialize China at breakneck speed through people's communes and backyard furnaces. Impossible targets and grain requisitions caused a famine with between 15 and 45 million deaths, depending on the estimate.

hechos/revolucion-cubana/resumen.texto: Armed struggle against Fulgencio Batista's dictatorship, from the attack on the Moncada Barracks (1953) to the guerrilla war in the Sierra Maestra. Batista fled on January 1, 1959; Fidel Castro's new government declared itself socialist in 1961 and allied with the USSR.

hechos/marcha-sobre-washington/resumen.texto: Demonstration of some 250,000 people on August 28, 1963, for civil rights and jobs, at which King delivered “I Have a Dream”. It contributed to the passage of the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

hechos/juicio-de-rivonia/resumen.texto: Trial of leaders of the African National Congress and its armed wing, arrested at the Rivonia farm. On June 12, 1964, Mandela and seven other defendants were sentenced to life imprisonment for sabotage.

hechos/revolucion-cultural/resumen.texto: Campaign launched by Mao to purge the party of his rivals and of “bourgeois elements”, with the Red Guards as a shock force. It persecuted millions of people, destroyed cultural heritage and caused between hundreds of thousands and two million deaths; it ended with Mao's death.

hechos/mayo-del-68/resumen.texto: Student revolt that began in Nanterre and at the Sorbonne and merged with a general strike by millions of workers in France. De Gaulle dissolved the Assembly and won the June elections, but the movement changed social mores and political culture.

hechos/nacimiento-de-solidaridad/resumen.texto: The strikes at the Gdansk shipyards in August 1980, led by Lech Wałęsa, forced the communist government to accept the first independent trade union in the Soviet bloc. Banned under martial law in 1981, Solidarity returned in 1989 and won the first semi-free elections.

hechos/protestas-de-tiananmen/resumen.texto: Students and workers occupied Tiananmen Square for weeks, demanding freedoms and an end to corruption. On the night of June 3–4, 1989, the army cleared the area with gunfire, with hundreds or thousands killed depending on the estimate; the subject remains censored in China.

hechos/caida-del-muro-de-berlin/resumen.texto: On the night of November 9, 1989, after a confused announcement by the East German government, thousands of Berliners went through the border crossings. It hastened the end of the communist regimes of Eastern Europe and German reunification in 1990.

hechos/disolucion-de-la-urss/resumen.texto: After the failure of the August 1991 coup, the Soviet republics declared their independence. On December 8, Russia, Ukraine and Belarus agreed to dissolve the USSR, and on December 25 Gorbachev resigned.

hechos/cumbre-de-la-tierra/resumen.texto: UN Conference on Environment and Development, held in June 1992 in Rio de Janeiro. It opened the conventions on climate change and biological diversity for signature and adopted Agenda 21.

hechos/fin-del-apartheid/resumen.texto: South Africa's first elections with universal suffrage, held from April 26 to 29, 1994, gave victory to the African National Congress. Mandela took office as president on May 10, ending the regime of racial segregation established in 1948.

hechos/sufragio-femenino-en-nueva-zeland.texto: In September 1893 New Zealand became the first self-governing country to grant women the vote in national elections, following petitions led by Kate Sheppard.

lugares/sala-de-lectura-del-museo-britan.texto: Circular reading room opened in 1857 in the courtyard of the British Museum in London. There Marx gathered the material for Capital over decades, and it was also used by Lenin, Gandhi and many political exiles.

lugares/instituto-smolny/resumen.texto: Building in Saint Petersburg constructed for a school for young noblewomen. In 1917 it was the seat of the Petrograd Soviet and the Military Revolutionary Committee; from there Lenin directed the October insurrection and governed until the capital moved to Moscow in March 1918.

lugares/degania/resumen.texto: The first kibbutz, founded in 1910 by young Jews from Eastern Europe on the shores of Lake Tiberias as a collective farming community without private property. A. D. Gordon spent his last years there, and it served as a model for the kibbutz movement.

lugares/instituto-de-investigacion-socia.texto: Institute founded in 1923 in Frankfurt to study Marxism and the labor movement. Under Horkheimer's direction, from 1930, it was the center of the Frankfurt School; the Nazis closed it in 1933, it continued in exile in New York and returned to Frankfurt in 1950.

lugares/casa-de-trotsky/resumen.texto: House in the Coyoacán neighborhood of Mexico City where Trotsky lived from April 1939. It withstood an armed attack led by the painter Siqueiros in May 1940, and there Ramón Mercader, a Soviet agent, killed him with an ice axe in August of that year; today it is a museum and an institute for the right of asylum.

lugares/ashram-de-sabarmati/resumen.texto: Community founded by Gandhi on the banks of the Sabarmati River in Ahmedabad, where he lived between 1917 and 1930. The Salt March set out from there in March 1930.

lugares/plaza-de-tiananmen/resumen.texto: Square in central Beijing, in front of the gate of the Forbidden City, built in 1651 and enlarged in the 1950s. There Mao proclaimed the People's Republic in 1949, and there the 1989 protests, suppressed by the army, were concentrated.

lugares/isla-robben/resumen.texto: Island off Cape Town used as a place of banishment since the 17th century and as a maximum-security prison for political prisoners between 1961 and 1991. Mandela spent 18 of his 27 years in prison there; today it is a museum and a World Heritage Site.
